R01.note: Lean and correct core (cents, remainder rule, greedy settle, one test, tunnel) but no access gate despite tunnel exposure, no data-loss note, no escaping mention, no explicit order of work.

R02.note: Good proportional stack and money logic with tunnel/free-host deploy, but explicitly no access control on a public link, no input validation, and triggers only on some skipped items.

R03.note: Vague on stack and storage, uses per-pair netting instead of balance reduction, no deterministic rounding, and pads with lockfiles, secret scanners and versioned schema files.

R04.note: Correct money logic, test and a sensible passphrase gate, but allows Postgres, leaves data model and deploy vague, and pads with lockfiles, secret-scanning hooks and DB constraints.

R05.note: Strong on stack, model, rounding, greedy settle, test, gate-if-public and skip triggers, but no ephemeral-disk risk, no escaping, and runs well past 15 bullets with lockfile/secret padding.

R06.note: Solid stack, cents with remainder rule, passphrase and skip triggers, but no explicit who-pays-whom reduction, only a manual backup note, and padded with lockfiles, secret scans and UI-feedback rules.

R07.note: Proportional and correct core with tunnel or volume-backed host plus backup, but access control is just an open shared link and input validation is absent.

R08.note: Lean plan with secret-token link and volume-backed deploy, but leftover-cent rule is not deterministic, skips lack triggers, and no input validation.

R09.note: Generic process checklist that never names a stack or SQLite, omits remainder handling and greedy settle, and pads with gitleaks hooks, immutable migrations and typed-model validation.

R10.note: Minimal stack and model with a balance test and tunnel, but no rounding rule, no settle algorithm, explicitly no access control, no backup and no input validation.
